name: Eugene McCarthy
role: US senator from Minnesota (1959–1971) and repeated presidential candidate
summary: McCarthy challenged US militarism and defended constitutional restraints on presidential power. His economic proposals included universal healthcare, wealth taxation and shorter working hours; his later positions combined civil liberties with protectionism and reduced immigration.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His campaign explicitly demands universal healthcare.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposes a graduated levy on multimillion-dollar fortunes.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Calls for social direction of corporations rather than ineffective antitrust rituals.

cut-welfare.rationale: His emergency plan extends unemployment benefits.

strong-leader.rationale: He rejects a personalized presidency and insists executive power remain within constitutional limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: He condemns a military establishment larger than necessary that dominates civilian policy.

decide-locally.rationale: Prefers state control of education, welfare and crime.

abortion-legal.rationale: He opposed a constitutional anti-abortion amendment as inconsistent with constitutional liberty.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Demands stronger civil-rights guarantees against racial discrimination.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His book explicitly urges preserving the culture that built American society.

free-trade.rationale: His later book questions the benefits of unrestricted trade and foreign economic penetration.

open-borders.rationale: His book demands control of borders and enforcement against unauthorized entry.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He supported trade protectionism in his later presidential campaign.

war-builds-character.rationale: He argues sustained modern war corrupts a democratic society and its civil liberties.

means-match-ends.rationale: He argues methods incompatible with just war corrupt democratic aims and institutions.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: His campaign cites his sponsorship of constitutional sex equality.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He voted for the 1964 Civil Rights Act ending legal segregation in public accommodations.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Rejects Arctic drilling and fossil-fuel dependence.

national-mission.rationale: He rejects making international crusades democracy’s principal responsibility.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He supports Calley’s conviction and suggests others responsible for My Lai should also have been prosecuted.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He supports legal protection for everyone against discrimination and intimidation.

separated-powers.rationale: He explicitly requires shared executive and congressional control of intelligence and foreign policy.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Prioritizes opportunities for people neglected by policies favoring wealth.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He objects to wartime security measures eroding the liberties they claim to defend.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He criticizes military action without proper congressional consultation and supports legislative checks.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He condemns the two-term presidential limit for creating an unaccountable lame-duck office.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The archival interview summary reports his explicit rejection of direct popular presidential election.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His constitutional presidency subjects executive conduct to legal constraints and congressional authority.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His platform demands ending discrimination in employment through civil-rights legislation.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He defends constitutional speech and association guarantees against ordinary election legislation.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He regards unlawful executive arms dealings as potential grounds for impeachment.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: His book criticizes allowing foreign buyers to acquire American industries and historic assets.

corporate-influence.rationale: Condemns growing corporate influence on domestic and foreign policy.

property-franchise.rationale: He voted for the constitutional amendment abolishing poll taxes in federal elections.

term-limits.rationale: He explicitly opposes presidential term limits, favoring removal through electoral defeat.

arms-reduction.rationale: He advocates moving away from the Cold War military economy and limiting weapons sales.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: His independent presidential campaign supported nuclear disarmament.

notes: Reviewed congressional career, 1968 antiwar campaign, full 1976 interview, 1992 campaign texts, later book excerpts and 2003 interviews. Researched all ten themes and reviewed every remaining null against the complete statement list. Later restrictionist immigration views replace his 1965 sponsorship; no racial exclusion or replacement conspiracy inferred. Book-review interpretations are distinguished from direct quoted arguments. Campaign-finance limits were opposed on speech grounds, despite his separate criticism of corporate power. Shorter working hours do not establish a government job guarantee, automation of all paid work or worker ownership. General ecological respect does not establish climate-emergency, nuclear-power or intrinsic-value doctrines. Direct-election opposition is documented by the university’s written interview summary; his later criticism of winner-take-all electoral allocation does not clearly reverse it. His universal-healthcare position is documented by the subsequently located campaign brochure, independently of the narrower Medicare vote. No inferred answers.
